blocks.text: 亮点

inlines.text: 亮点
Beam 1.0 501B-A23B：
一个仅解码器 MoE，采用滑动窗口和全注意力，256 个路由专家和 top-8 选择，以及原生 1M token 上下文窗口。
检查点支持：
BF16、ModelOpt NVFP4 和 compressed-tensors 动态 FP8。
服务特性：
DFlash2 投机解码、基数缓存和 HiCache、分块预填充、CUDA graphs、TP/EP/PP 和注意力数据并行。
内核优化：
投影打包、跨注意力和残差边界的融合、用于 FP32 路由器的专用 BF16x3 GEMM，以及 GB300 MoE 调优。
性能：
在 4 块 NVIDIA GB300 GPU 上使用 NVFP4 检查点进行 OpenHands 多轮智能体编码回放时，SGLang 在并发 32 下达到每 GPU 127.6K 总 token/秒，每用户 185.87 token/秒（p50）。

inlines.text: 融合优化

blocks.text: Beam 的归一化和门控路径围绕投影和集合通信串联起一系列小操作。我们融合这些链以消除中间存储、拷贝和启动开销。

inlines.text: Beam 的归一化和门控路径围绕投影和集合通信串联起一系列小操作。我们融合这些链以消除中间存储、拷贝和启动开销。
跨投影、归一化和集合通信边界的核融合。

我们融合 all-reduce、输出归一化、缩放残差加法和下一输入归一化，将可融合边界扩展到 NVFP4。PDL 让后续归一化在其依赖等待之前加载权重。滑动层将 Q/K 归一化与 RoPE 融合。完整注意力层使用融合的 Q/K 归一化并复用 SSMax 位置缩放。符合条件的 BF16 层将 QKV 和门控投影打包为一次启动。注意力门控融合偏置加法、sigmoid 和乘法。BF16 MoE 集合通信路径还集成了本地专家求和、路由缩放和 BF16 舍入。
使用 MegaMoE 结合专家通信与计算。

我们在 FlashInfer MegaMoE 上启用 Beam 的 NVFP4 专家，将其 runner 与 MegaMoE all-to-all 后端配对。FlashInfer 在其融合 EP 核内执行专家分发、计算和合并。Beam 提供显式专家 ID 和路由权重，并接收每个 rank 令牌的完整输出。融合转换在加法之前保留两个缩放残差操作数的舍入。注意力和 MoE 有各自独立的融合资格检查；MoE 归约遵循所选后端的所有权。CPU 卸载、空流水线阶段和不支持的集合通信形状保留常规路径。所有 EP rank 都参与专家执行，包括没有本地令牌的 rank。

inlines.text: Miles 中的强化学习

blocks.text: Miles 通过 Megatron 插件支持 Beam，并在 Reflection 的 SGLang 构建上运行 rollout。 训练后端实现了 Beam 的三明治归一化与深度缩放残差、 SSMax 注意力缩放、混合滑动窗口注意力、门控注意力输出、 无辅助损失的 MoE 路由，以及 FP32 最终 logit 软上限，并通过 Megatron-Bridge 直接加载 Hugging Face 检查点。目标是让同一响应的训练器与 rollout 对数概率尽可能接近。

blocks.text: 并行性。 后端支持 DP、TP、SP、EP、专家 TP 和 PP。TP 对 注意力投影（包括输出门）进行分片，SP 则沿序列维度对它们之间的激活进行分片。EP 和专家 TP 独立于 注意力布局对路由专家进行分片，流水线阶段可以容纳不等数量的层。启用路由重放后， 训练器–rollout 差距在这些布局下保持同一水平， 且不会随训练步数增长。

blocks.text: 路由重放。 Rollout Routing Replay 作为可选项提供。SGLang 记录每个生成 token 所选的专家，训练器的 MoE 层复用这些分配，而不是重新计算 top-k，因此近乎并列的路由器分数不会在训练中选择不同的专家路径。重放的路由在激活重计算期间以及每个流水线阶段也会生效。

blocks.text: 数值一致性。 在 Beam 对精度敏感的地方，训练器遵循 SGLang 的数值处理。最终 logit 软上限以 FP32 运行，深度缩放残差加法在与引擎融合内核相同的点进行舍入。路由器门在训练、检查点和权重同步过程中始终保持 FP32。这些改动共同将训练器–rollout 对数概率差距减半，使其处于 BF16 归约顺序噪声的水平。确定性设置使重复运行可复现。

blocks.text: 共置与分离部署。 Beam 可在任一模式下运行。分离式运行将训练和 rollout 放在不同的 GPU 上，并将下一次 rollout 与当前训练步重叠；TIS 缓解由此产生的一步策略陈旧所导致的离策略不匹配。共置运行共享相同的 GPU 并同步交替进行，在引擎生成时将训练器状态卸载到节点本地 NVMe。在两种模式下，更新后的 BF16 权重在每一步之后以桶的形式传输到引擎。

blocks.text: SGLang now supports Beam natively and powers Reflection’s production API. It helps developers translate Beam’s inference efficiency into practical and production-proven serving performance. BF16, NVFP4, and dynamic FP8 support provide flexibility across precision and memory requirements; DFlash2 speculative decoding accelerates generation; and prefix caching with hybrid-attention memory management enables efficient reuse of context across agent interactions. Underneath these serving capabilities, we optimized Beam’s projections, normalization, and communication to improve throughput.

blocks.text: Highlights

inlines.text: Highlights
Beam 1.0 501B-A23B:
a decoder-only MoE with sliding-window and full attention, 256 routed experts and top-8 selection, and a native 1M-token context window.
Checkpoint support:
BF16, ModelOpt NVFP4, and compressed-tensors dynamic FP8.
Serving features:
DFlash2 speculative decoding, radix caching and HiCache, chunked prefill, CUDA graphs, TP/EP/PP and attention data parallelism.
Kernel optimizations:
projection packing, fusion across attention and residual boundaries, a specialized BF16x3 GEMM for FP32 router, and GB300 MoE tuning.
Performance:

On an OpenHands multi-turn agentic coding replay with the NVFP4 checkpoint on 4 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs, SGLang reaches 127.6K total tokens/sec per GPU at 185.87 tokens/sec per user (p50) with concurrency 32.

blocks.text: Hybrid Attention and Output Gating

inlines.text: Hybrid Attention and Output Gating

blocks.text: GQA shares eight KV heads among 48 query heads, reducing the KV cache that SGLang stores per token. Sliding-window layers also restrict their live history to the recent window and use RoPE. Full-attention layers use NoPE with position-dependent SSMax query scaling. Both normalize Q and K before attention.

blocks.text: Beam gates the attention result before the output projection. A second projection produces gate activations from the normalized hidden state; the model adds a learned per-head bias, applies sigmoid, and multiplies the attention output by the elementwise gate. The QKV and gate projections share an input, which lets us pack them into one BF16 projection in eligible layouts.

blocks.text: Beam’s full-attention layers use Scalable Softmax (SSMax) to keep attention focused as context grows. After Q/K normalization, each query at zero-based position p is scaled by (1+(p+1)/2048)0.1. This gradually sharpens the attention distribution, counteracting the tendency for softmax weights to spread across more tokens in long contexts.

blocks.text: Fusion Optimizations

inlines.text: Fusion Optimizations

blocks.text: Beam's normalization and gating paths chain small operations around the projections and collectives. We fuse these chains to remove intermediate stores, copies and launches.

inlines.text: Beam's normalization and gating paths chain small operations around the projections and collectives. We fuse these chains to remove intermediate stores, copies and launches.
Kernel Fusion across projections, normalization, and collective boundaries.

We fuse all-reduce, output norm, scaled residual addition and next input norm, extending eligible boundaries to NVFP4. PDL lets the following norm load weights before its dependency wait. Sliding layers fuse Q/K normalization with RoPE. Full-attention layers use fused Q/K normalization and reuse SSMax position scales. Eligible BF16 layers pack QKV and gate projections into one launch. Attention gating fuses bias addition, sigmoid and multiplication. The BF16 MoE collective path also incorporates local expert summation, routed scaling and BF16 rounding.
Combine expert communication and compute with MegaMoE.

We enable Beam's NVFP4 experts on FlashInfer MegaMoE, pairing its runner with the MegaMoE all-to-all backend. FlashInfer runs expert dispatch, computation and combine inside its fused EP kernel. Beam supplies explicit expert IDs and routing weights and receives complete outputs for each rank's tokens. The fused transitions preserve the rounding of both scaled residual operands before addition. Attention and MoE have separate fusion eligibility checks; MoE reduction follows the selected backend's ownership. CPU offload, empty pipeline stages and unsupported collective shapes retain the regular paths. All EP ranks participate in expert execution, including ranks with no local tokens.

inlines.text: Reinforcement learning in Miles

blocks.text: Miles supports Beam through a Megatron plugin and runs rollouts on Reflection's SGLang build. The training backend implements Beam's sandwich normalization with depth-scaled residuals, SSMax attention scaling, hybrid sliding-window attention, gated attention output, auxiliary-loss-free MoE routing, and FP32 final-logit softcapping, and loads the Hugging Face checkpoint directly through Megatron-Bridge. The goal is to keep trainer and rollout log-probabilities for the same responses as close as possible.

blocks.text: Parallelism. The backend supports DP, TP, SP, EP, expert TP, and PP. TP shards the attention projections, including the output gate, and SP shards the activations between them along the sequence. EP and expert TP shard the routed experts independently of the attention layout, and pipeline stages can hold unequal numbers of layers. With routing replay enabled, the trainer–rollout gap stays at the same level across these layouts and does not grow over training steps.

inlines.text: Parallelism.

The backend supports DP, TP, SP, EP, expert TP, and PP. TP shards the attention projections, including the output gate, and SP shards the activations between them along the sequence. EP and expert TP shard the routed experts independently of the attention layout, and pipeline stages can hold unequal numbers of layers. With routing replay enabled, the trainer–rollout gap stays at the same level across these layouts and does not grow over training steps.

blocks.text: Routing replay. Rollout Routing Replay is available as an opt-in. SGLang records the experts selected for each generated token, and the trainer's MoE layers reuse those assignments instead of recomputing top-k, so near-tied router scores cannot select a different expert path in training. Replayed routes also apply during activation recomputation and on every pipeline stage.

blocks.text: Numerical consistency. The trainer follows SGLang's numerics wherever Beam is precision-sensitive. The final-logit softcap runs in FP32, and depth-scaled residual additions round at the same points as the engine's fused kernel. The router gate stays in FP32 through training, checkpointing, and weight synchronization. Together these changes halve the trainer–rollout log-probability gap, leaving it at the level of BF16 reduction-order noise. Deterministic settings make repeated runs reproducible.

blocks.text: Colocated and disaggregated deployment. Beam runs in either mode. Disaggregated runs place training and rollout on separate GPUs and overlap the next rollout with the current training step; TIS mitigates the off-policy mismatch resulting from this one-step policy staleness. Colocated runs share the same GPUs and alternate synchronously, offloading trainer state to node-local NVMe while the engines generate. In both modes, updated BF16 weights are transferred to the engines in buckets after each step.

inlines.text: OpenHands Agentic Coding Sweep

blocks.text: We collected performance results for Beam NVFP4 on four GB300 GPUs with TP4 using an OpenHands multi-turn agentic coding workload. Each conversation starts with an around 74K token prompt and outputs around 220 tokens each turn, for a total of 13 turns. Successive turns reuse the prefix for a ~92% aggregate cache hit rate. We sweep concurrency across 1, 4, 8, 16, and 32 conversations and plot per-GPU token throughput (tok/s/GPU) against p50 interactivity (tok/s/user). Total throughput includes cached input tokens. These measurements use eight-token DFlash2 blocks with simulated acceptance length fixed at four and real draft tokens; they do not measure natural draft acceptance or model accuracy.

blocks.text: AgentX Agentic Coding Sweep

inlines.text: AgentX Agentic Coding Sweep

blocks.text: In collaboration with NVIDIA, we collected performance results for Beam NVFP4 on four GB300 GPUs with TP4/EP1 using AgentX, SemiAnalysis's replayer for recorded multi-turn agentic coding traces. AgentX reproduces the prompt sizes, prefix sharing, subagent fan-out and inter-turn timing of real coding-agent sessions, so the results reflect "realistic agentic load". Requests in a session share a long prefix, so 92% to 96% of input tokens hit the prefix cache. FP8 KV cache was utilized, and the selected speculative block size was 8. We sweep concurrency from 1 to 96 sessions and plot per-GPU token throughput (tok/s/GPU) against p90 interactivity (tok/s/user). At concurrency 96, throughput reaches 83,504 tok/s/GPU at 43.9 tok/s/user; a single session runs at 348.0 tok/s/user.
